cues.en: Have you ever wondered what's inside one of these electric car chargers? Well then, this is the video for you. The short answer is… not a lot really. The longer answer has to do with how electric vehicles charge themselves, because this isn't actually a charger. The industry name for this device is EVSE, which stands for Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment. Kinda weird that we're calling it an equipment, but let's not get any more pedantic than this video is already guaranteed to be.
cues.zh: 你有没有想过这些电动汽车充电器里面到底有什么？那这期视频就是为你准备的。简短的回答是……其实没什么东西。长一点的回答则跟电动汽车如何充电有关，因为这其实根本不是充电器。这个设备在行业里的名称是EVSE，代表电动汽车供电设备。管它叫“设备”有点奇怪，但咱们就别比这期视频本身更吹毛求疵了。

cues.en: Fundamentally, this device is merely a controlled access point to the power grid. I've been wanting to make this video for a long time, but finally got motivated to do it thanks to a series of interactions on Twitter. You know who you are. First, qualifications. This video is discussing Level 2 AC charging in North America.
cues.zh: 从根本上说，这个设备只是一个受控的电网接入点。我早就想做这期视频了，但终于在Twitter上的一系列互动之后有了动力。你们知道我说的是谁。先说前提。这期视频讨论的是北美的Level 2交流充电。

cues.en: Those of you with your fancy 3-phases need not comment on your Type 2 connectors because, yes, I know they exist in Europe, Australia, and elsewhere, but they do not exist over here, so mentioning them is irrelevant. DC fast charging, the most famous system of which being the Tesla Superchargers, is not where we're headed either. Not today, anyway. Instead, this video is about quote-unquote slow, at-home, or at-the-office charging, and the devices which make that work.
cues.zh: 你们那些用着高级三相电的人就别在评论区提你们的Type 2接口了，因为，是的，我知道欧洲、澳大利亚和其他地方有，但这边没有，所以提它们无关紧要。直流快充——其中最著名的系统是Tesla Superchargers——也不是我们要讲的内容。至少今天不是。相反，这期视频讲的是所谓的慢速、在家或在办公室充电，以及让这一切运作起来的设备。

cues.en: Unless you plan on exceeding your vehicle's range in a day, in other words, are doing long-distance travel, this is how the vast majority of your charging will, and in my humble opinion, should occur.
cues.zh: 除非你打算一天内超出车辆的续航里程，换句话说，要跑长途，否则这就是你绝大多数充电会发生、而且依我浅见应该发生的方式。

cues.en: I very much hope we focus on getting more level 2 chargers in more places to help accommodate those who need a car but don't live in a single family home, rather than make that huge percentage of the population reliance on DC fast charging, thus replicating the fueling infrastructure we have today but with high speed chargers instead of gas pumps.
cues.zh: 我非常希望我们能专注于在更多地方安装更多的二级充电器，以帮助那些需要汽车但不住在单户家庭住宅中的人，而不是让这一庞大比例的人口依赖直流快速充电，从而复制我们今天拥有的燃料补给基础设施，只不过用高速充电器代替了加油泵。

cues.en: Plugging in at home or at work is not only much more convenient, but requires less radical infrastructure and from my perspective seems a lot easier to manage on a connected smart grid. But the main reason why I hope we go with the more level 2, less DC charging route is because these things are stupidly simple devices. I said earlier that these aren't chargers. In fact, these are basically just fancy light switches.
cues.zh: 在家中或工作地点插电充电不仅更加方便，而且需要的激进基础设施更少，从我的角度来看，在互联智能电网上管理起来似乎容易得多。但我希望我们选择更多二级充电、更少直流充电路线的主要原因是，这些东西是简单到令人发指的装置。我之前说过，这些不是充电器。事实上，这些基本上只是花哨的电灯开关。

cues.en: Let's explain what I mean. Most things we call chargers are really DC power supplies. Yes, even those aren't often really chargers. They contain electronic circuitry designed to turn AC mains voltage into a defined and stable DC voltage. In the case of standard USB, that would be 5 volts. The charging is done by the device you give the 5 volts to, because it knows how to treat its battery best.
cues.zh: 让我解释一下我的意思。我们称之为充电器的大多数东西实际上是直流电源。是的，即使那些也往往不是真正的充电器。它们包含电子电路，旨在将交流市电电压转换为定义明确的稳定直流电压。对于标准USB来说，那就是5伏。充电是由你提供5伏电压的设备完成的，因为它知道如何最好地对待自己的电池。

cues.en: Electric cars are pretty much the same. In the case of level 1 and 2 charging, they handle the charging themselves. But they go one step further than your phone or laptop. Because electric vehicles come in all sorts of shapes, sizes, battery chemistries, and battery pack voltages, it's not really feasible to put the power supply outside of the car. So it isn't. This device has no voltage conversion circuitry in it of any kind, except for the wee bit it needs for its own electronics.
cues.zh: 电动汽车也是如此。在1级和2级充电的情况下，它们自己处理充电。但它们比你的手机或笔记本电脑更进一步。因为电动汽车有各种形状、尺寸、电池化学和电池组电压，所以把电源放在车外并不真正可行。所以它不在外面。这个设备里面没有任何电压转换电路，除了它自身电子设备需要的一点点。

cues.en: A reminder to the keyboard warriors out there, we're not talking about DC fast charging in this video. This device has one job and one job only. To safely deliver AC power to a car. The car itself contains the battery charger. Want to see it? Well, in the Chevy Bolt EV, it's here. These four boxes represent all of the electrical bits of a Bolt. The Bolt bits.
cues.zh: 键盘侠们注意了，本期视频我们不聊直流快充。这个设备只干一件事，而且只干一件事：安全地把交流电送到车上。充电机其实在车里面。想看吗？在Chevy Bolt EV里，它在这儿。这四个盒子代表了Bolt的所有电气部件。Bolt的部件。

cues.en: Up on top here to the left is a junction box which splits out traction battery voltage to the inverter module and high power accessories like the air conditioning compressor and cabin heater. Below it is the inverter module which actually drives the traction motor and thus wheels and recovers charge under regenerative braking. On the right up top you have a DC-DC converter which takes high traction battery voltage and steps it down to 13.8 volts or so to power accessories and charge the 12 volt battery,
cues.zh: 左上方是一个接线盒，它把动力电池电压分配给逆变器模块和空调压缩机、座舱加热器这类大功率附件。它下面是逆变器模块，负责驱动牵引电机，进而驱动车轮，并在能量回收制动时回收电量。右上方是一个DC-DC转换器，它把高电压的动力电池电压降压到13.8伏左右，为附件供电并给12伏电池充电，

cues.en: In other words, this is the equivalent of an alternator in a conventional car, and below it is the onboard charger. Side note, a lot of you may be asking why an electric car needs a standard 12 volt lead acid battery. Technically it doesn't need it, but the design of the car becomes much safer and also easier if you can run conventional things like lighting, infotainment, power windows, the computers, etc. off of low voltage.
cues.zh: 换句话说，这相当于传统汽车里的发电机，它下面是车载充电机。顺便说一句，很多人可能会问，电动车为什么还需要一块标准的12伏铅酸电池。严格来说并不需要，但如果能让照明、信息娱乐、电动车窗、电脑等常规设备都跑在低压下，整车设计会安全得多，也简单得多。

cues.en: It's easier because it means the things that are the same from a gas car to an EV don't need to change. Imagine a 400 volt turn signal bulb. And it's safer because, well for one, you don't have high voltage wiring running all over the place, but more importantly, when the car is off and not charging, contactors inside the battery open, removing traction battery voltage from everything. What are contactors? Well, you'll find out shortly.
cues.zh: 说简单，是因为从燃油车到电动车都一样的那些东西不用改。想象一下400伏的转向灯灯泡。说安全，一是因为高压线不用满车乱跑，更重要的是，当车辆熄火且不在充电时，电池内部的接触器会断开，把动力电池电压从所有部件上切除。什么是接触器？你很快就会知道。

cues.en: You can actually hear those contactors close when you turn on the car, or plug it in. And obviously when the high voltage system is shut down, you need something else to close those contactors and turn it back on. And that's why the bulk of the car's control systems run at the conventional 12 volts, and why there's a standard battery too.
cues.zh: 你启动汽车或插上电源时，其实能听到那些接触器闭合的声音。显然，当高压系统关闭时，你需要别的办法来闭合这些接触器并重新启动。这就是为什么汽车的大部分控制系统采用传统的12伏电压，也是为什么还有一个标准电池。

cues.en: Anyway, again, this is the onboard charger. It's kind of hard to see in situ. If you'd like a closer look at these components, I can't recommend this video from the Weber Automotive YouTube channel highly enough. It's fantastic. Also, everything is a lot cleaner. But this module here is the actual charger. It takes AC power coming from the car's charge port, rectifies it to DC, boosts that up to the battery pack's required charge voltage, and sends that into the battery pack.
cues.zh: 总之，再说一次，这是车载充电器。在原位很难看清楚。如果你想更仔细地看这些组件，我强烈推荐Weber Automotive YouTube频道的这个视频。非常棒。而且，一切都干净得多。但这里的这个模块才是真正的充电器。它接收从汽车充电口进来的交流电，整流成直流电，升压到电池组所需的充电电压，然后送入电池组。

cues.en: Inside the pack itself, you've also got various modules which monitor each cell and help balance everything out. Now here's where things get a little complicated and where the critical role of the EVSE comes in. The car's onboard charger may be capable of pulling more power from the grid than a given circuit can safely provide. It's the EVSE's job to tell the car how much current it can pull and then to supply it with voltage when requested. Let's now take a closer look at the device itself.
cues.zh: 在电池组内部，你还有各种模块，监测每个电芯并帮助平衡一切。现在，事情变得有点复杂，也是EVSE的关键作用所在。汽车的车载充电器可能能够从电网汲取超过给定电路安全提供的电力。EVSE的职责是告诉汽车可以汲取多少电流，然后在需要时为其提供电压。现在让我们更仔细地看看这个设备本身。

cues.en: This is a Siemens VersaCharge unit, a fairly basic EVSE. It has a NEMA 650 plug on one end, and the industry standard SAE J1772 connector on the other. Since 2010,
cues.zh: 这是一个西门子 VersaCharge 充电桩，是一款相当基础的电动汽车供电设备（EVSE）。它的一端是一个 NEMA 650 插头，另一端是行业标准的 SAE J1772 连接器。自 2010 年以来，

cues.en: Every single battery-electric vehicle and plug-in hybrid for sale in the US that doesn't begin with T and end in Tesla has this very connector on it. From the Chevy Volt, the Ford Focus Electric, the Nissan Leaf, the Volkswagen e-Golf, the Toyota Prius Prime, the Kia Soul EV, the Hyundai Kona Electric, and yes, even the WeGo Life… they
cues.zh: 美国所有在售的纯电动汽车和插电式混合动力车，只要不是以 T 开头、以 Tesla 结尾的，都带有这个连接器。从雪佛兰 Volt、福特 Focus Electric、日产 Leaf、大众 e-Golf、丰田普锐斯 Prime、起亚 Soul EV、现代 Kona Electric，到没错，甚至还有 WeGo Life……它们

cues.en: all have this charge port. This connector is part of the universal nationwide, except for Tesla, levels 1 and 2 charging standard, capable of delivering up to just shy of 20 kilowatts, though typically most units deliver between 6 and 7.2. This unit, like many out there, is rated for 30 amps, so depending on the voltage it receives, it can deliver between 6.2 and 7.2 kilowatts.
cues.zh: 都配有这个充电接口。这个连接器是全美通用（特斯拉除外）1 级和 2 级充电标准的一部分，最高可输送近 20 千瓦的功率，不过通常大多数设备的功率在 6 到 7.2 千瓦之间。这个设备和市面上许多设备一样，额定电流为 30 安培，因此根据它接收的电压，可以提供 6.2 到 7.2 千瓦的功率。

cues.en: We find a user interface on the front of this device, though not all EVSEs are going to have one. The most useful thing this does is allow you to delay charging for up to eight hours in two-hour increments, a fairly easy way to take advantage of time of use rates if your utility offers them. Though it should be noted, most cars can do this themselves. In fact, on the Bolt EV, you can even program that based on GPS location so it charges immediately when on a public charger, but only between certain times at home.
cues.zh: 我们在设备正面可以看到一个用户界面，不过并非所有 EVSE 都有这个功能。这其中最实用的功能是允许你以两小时为单位延迟长达八小时充电，如果你的电力公司提供分时电价，这是一种相当简便的利用方式。不过需要指出的是，大多数汽车本身就能做到这一点。事实上，在 Bolt EV 上，你甚至可以根据 GPS 位置进行编程，这样它在公共充电桩上就会立即充电，而在家里则只在特定时间段充电。

cues.en: A lot of the symbology on here is, I believe, shared between multiple models because I don't think this unit has any sort of Wi-Fi connectivity. Though frankly, I don't really care either way. Oh, and of course it has fancy lights on it because what good is driving an electric vehicle if you don't get to be smug about it?
cues.zh: 这里很多符号标识，我觉得是多个型号共用的，因为我认为这个设备没有任何 Wi-Fi 连接功能。不过说实话，我对此也不太在意。哦，当然它上面还有炫酷的灯，毕竟开电动车如果不能沾沾自喜，那还有什么意思呢？

cues.en: Let's now open it up. You might be surprised to learn that most of what's in here is simply empty space. The unit is way larger than it actually needs to be, partly so it can have those fancy lights to help your smugness, and partly because it helps manage the cord when not in use. The power leads from the plug
cues.zh: 现在咱们把它打开。你可能会惊讶地发现，里面大部分其实只是空荡荡的空间。这个设备比实际需要的尺寸大得多，一部分是为了装那些炫酷的灯来助长你的得意劲儿，另一部分是为了在不使用时方便收纳线缆。插头的电源线

cues.en: which interestingly are not colored properly, the white wire should be red since there is no neutral but whatever, go to a terminal block allowing you to replace the plug or hardwire the unit if so desired. One reason to do that is that this particular model is weatherproofed and so can be outside if installed and wired properly. From there a few small feeders go to the circuit board and two large conductors go to one side of a contactor.
cues.zh: 有意思的是，颜色标得并不规范，白色线应该是红色的，因为没有零线，不过无所谓了，这些线接到接线端子上，让你可以更换插头或者直接硬接线。这么做的一个原因是，这个型号本身是防风雨的，所以如果安装和接线得当，可以放在户外。从那里，几根细馈线接到电路板，两根粗导线接到接触器的一侧。

cues.en: Out the other side of the contactor, you'll see that it goes to the main conductors of the charge cable. This contactor is the single control device of this unit. A contactor is simply an electromagnetic switch. When energized, it closes, connecting the charge cord directly to incoming power. When it's open, it doesn't. That's it. That's all these devices do. They're a fancy light switch.
cues.zh: 从接触器的另一侧出来，你会看到它连接到充电线缆的主导线。这个接触器是该设备唯一的控制器件。接触器就是一个电磁开关。通电时它闭合，把充电线直接连到输入电源上。断开时就不连通。就这么简单。这些设备就干这个。它们就是个高级的电灯开关。

cues.en: But it is a critical safety device and what keeps your car from overloading a circuit. Let's talk about that part first. Keep in mind that the car is the load. The charger is inside the car. This device is simply a gateway to the grid. It is labeled as though it's a 30 amp device which makes things easier for regulators and electricians, but in reality the device itself consumes maybe 5 watts. The car is where the load actually comes from.
cues.zh: 但这是一个关键的安全装置，它能防止你的车让电路过载。我们先来说说这个部分。记住，车才是负载。充电器在车里面。这个设备只是通往电网的关口。它被标称为30安的设备，这样便于监管机构和电工处理，但实际上这个设备本身只消耗大约5瓦。负载其实来自车。

cues.en: So first and foremost, it needs to tell the car how much power it can safely pull. The device can only supply 30 amps because it's on a 40 amp circuit. Technically it's allowed to provide up to 32 continuously, and truthfully I don't know why they capped it at 30, but anyway, the device needs to tell the car, hey, don't pull more than 30 amps, you'll make trouble if you do. And it does that through very rudimentary signaling protocols.
cues.zh: 所以首先，它需要告诉车能安全地取用多少电。这个设备最多只能提供30安，因为它接在40安的电路上。严格来说，它允许持续提供高达32安，说实话我也不知道为什么他们把它限制在30安，但无论如何，这个设备需要告诉车：嘿，别取超过30安，否则会出问题。它是通过非常基础的信号协议来实现这一点的。

cues.en: So here's a close up of the pins on the car's side. And now on the plug's side. This one helpfully labels which pin is which. The three largest pins are line 1, line 2, slash neutral, and a safety ground, or protective earth. If you're confused on why pin 2 is only sometimes neutral, you might want to check out this video I recently made on the US electrical system. In short, we use split phase power, and on a 240 or 208 volt circuit, both pins will be hot, but on a 120 volt circuit, only one of them is.
cues.zh: 这是车这一侧引脚的近景。现在看插头这一侧。这个插头贴心地标注了哪个引脚是哪个。三个最大的引脚分别是线1、线2/零线，以及安全接地或保护地。如果你对为什么引脚2有时才是零线感到困惑，你可能想看看我最近制作的关于美国电力系统的视频。简而言之，我们使用分相电力，在240或208伏的电路上，两个引脚都是火线，但在120伏的电路上，只有其中一个是火线。

cues.en: The other smaller pins are the control pilot and the proximity pilot. Let's start with proximity. The main purpose of these pins is to tell the car and the EVSE that they're connected to each other. On the EVSE side, the proximity pilot and ground pin are connected via a resistor which allows the car to know it's plugged into an EVSE, even in the event the EVSE is dead.
cues.zh: 另外几个较小的引脚是控制导引引脚和接近导引引脚。先从接近导引说起。这些引脚的主要作用是告诉车辆和EVSE（充电设备）它们已经彼此连接。在EVSE一侧，接近导引引脚和接地引脚通过一个电阻相连，这样即使EVSE断电，车辆也能知道已插入EVSE。

cues.en: This completely passive method ensures that when the car is plugged in, even if the EVSE is faulty or there's no power to it, it knows it's connected to an EVSE and won't let you shift from park. A well thought out design preventing the careless from driving away with the charge point. The control pilot is a little more complicated but still not all that much. If it's a weight and ready to charge, the EVSE puts a 1kHz square wave signal out on the control pilot pin.
cues.zh: 这种完全被动的方式确保车辆插入时，即便EVSE故障或无电，车辆也知道连接到了EVSE，不会让你从驻车挡移出。这是考虑周到的设计，防止粗心者带着充电枪开车离开。控制导引稍复杂些，但也不算太复杂。如果准备就绪可以充电，EVSE会在控制导引引脚上发出1kHz方波信号。

cues.en: Without a car plugged in, that circuit is open, so nothing happens at all. But when a car is plugged in, just as there's a resistor on the EVSE side for the car, there's a resistor on the car for the EVSE side. In fact, the car can manipulate the resistance in order to signal different things to the EVSE. Per the spec, when the car is connected, it should have a 2740 ohm resistance across the protective earth and the control pilot pin. This signals presence to the EVSE.
cues.zh: 未插入车辆时，该电路是断开的，所以什么也不会发生。但当车辆插入时，正如EVSE侧有给车辆的电阻，车辆侧也有给EVSE的电阻。实际上，车辆可以调节电阻值，向EVSE发送不同信号。按规范，车辆连接时，保护接地与控制导引引脚之间应有2740欧姆电阻，以此向EVSE表明车辆已连接。

cues.en: To request power, the car lowers that resistance value down to 882 ohms. That will cause the EVSE to close the contactor, and none the vehicle can charge. There is also a very special and rare case where the car will lower the pilot circuit resistance further to 246 ohms to signal that it requires ventilation when charging. This is used to prevent such a hypothetical vehicle from being charged indoors. I'm not aware of—
cues.zh: 要请求供电，车辆会把电阻值降到882欧姆。这会让EVSE闭合接触器，然后车辆才能充电。还有一种非常特殊且罕见的情况：车辆会把引导电路电阻进一步降到246欧姆，表示充电时需要通风。这是为了防止这种假设中的车辆在室内充电。据我所知——

cues.en: any consumer-facing applications where this is in use, but if you were ever wondering why your charger says ventilation not required on there, that's why. Is to prevent such a car, perhaps one with lead acid batteries which could produce a lot of hydrogen when charging? Really not sure what would require ventilation. But anyway, to prevent such a car from being charged with this supply.
cues.zh: 没有任何面向消费者的应用在使用这个功能，但如果你曾好奇为什么你的充电器上写着“无需通风”，原因就在这里。是为了防止这种车——也许是装有铅酸电池、充电时可能产生大量氢气的车——被充电。真不确定什么情况会需要通风。但总之，是为了防止这种车用这个供电设备充电。

cues.en: Most importantly though, that one kilohertz square wave being sent on the control pilot pin is pulse width modulated to signal the maximum charge current the car is permitted to take. That is arguably the single most important thing the EVSE does. See, a Chevy Bolt has a 7.2 kilowatt onboard charger. That happens to match the rating of this EVSE so we're all hunky dory. But what if I wanted to charge it on a smaller circuit?
cues.zh: 不过最重要的是，控制引导引脚上发送的那1千赫兹方波经过脉宽调制，用来告知车辆允许抽取的最大充电电流。这可以说是EVSE最重要的功能。你看，雪佛兰Bolt有一个7.2千瓦的车载充电器。恰好和这个EVSE的额定值匹配，所以皆大欢喜。但如果我想把它接到更小的电路上充电呢？

cues.en: Say I had installed a 3.6kW charger on a 20A circuit. The car needs to know it's only allowed to pull 3.6kW, or else it would overload the circuit and trip the breaker. Which is of course inconvenient, but also you're then relying on the breaker to actually trip, and if it's faulty you could very well have a fire on your hands. Better to not tempt fate. The EVSE is also monitoring the circuit for any ground faults and will open the contactor should one occur.
cues.zh: 假设我在20安培电路上装了一个3.6千瓦的充电器。车辆需要知道它只能抽取3.6千瓦，否则就会使电路过载并跳闸。这当然很不方便，而且你还得指望断路器真的会跳闸，如果它坏了，你很可能就面临火灾了。最好别去试探命运。EVSE还会监测电路是否有接地故障，一旦发生就会断开接触器。

cues.en: They're usually designed to self-reset at least a few times so that you aren't left without a charge in the morning, and they'll also self-test things like the integrity of the protective earth and provide other various protections. But at a core level, all this does is announce its presence and capacity and wait for a signal to initiate charging. Then it goes, and the car does the rest. So if these are merely fancy light switches, why are they so gosh darn expensive?
cues.zh: 它们通常设计为至少能自我重置几次，这样你早上就不会没电可用；它们还会自检保护接地是否完好，并提供其他各种保护。但在核心层面上，这一切只是宣告自身的存在和容量，然后等待信号启动充电。接着它就开始工作，剩下的由车辆完成。那么，如果这些不过是高级电灯开关，为什么还这么贵得离谱？

cues.en: It's not exactly hyperbole to say the functions of this EVSE could be replicated with an Arduino, a contactor from an air conditioning unit, a power supply, and a willing middle schooler. The answer? Ehhhhhh. Okay, well, in fairness, there are plenty of options these days which can provide all that this car can take for around $300. The greatest cost of installing a charging station will always be simply running a new circuit to wherever you need it to be.
cues.zh: 说这台EVSE的功能可以用一个Arduino、一个空调机组里的接触器、一个电源和一个愿意动手的中学生来复现，这并不算夸张。答案？呃……好吧，公平地说，如今有很多选择，花大约300美元就能提供这辆车能接受的全部功能。安装充电站的最大成本永远只是把新电路拉到你需要的位置。

cues.en: which is why it would be great if we could require at least one 40 amp 240 volt circuit for garages in new building codes. But anyway, the charger itself need not be expensive because it's a pretty dumb device. I believe I've said this a few times now, but it is basically a fancy light switch. The greatest cost in these units is almost certainly the charge cable itself. It's a fairly specialized and quite beefy multi-conductor cable, built to withstand a fair bit of abuse.
cues.zh: 所以，如果能在新建筑规范中要求车库至少配备一条40安培240伏的电路，那就太好了。但无论如何，充电器本身不必昂贵，因为它是个相当笨的设备。我想我已经说过几次了，它基本上就是个高级电灯开关。这些单元中最大的成本几乎肯定是充电线本身。它是一根相当专用、相当粗壮的多芯电缆，能承受不少折腾。

cues.en: This entire unit weighs something like 20 pounds or roughly 9 kilograms, but the vast majority of that is just this cable. The actual unit is a plastic box. The connector itself is designed for 10,000 insertion removal events, which means it should last a couple of decades in a private setting and a good few years at least in a public one. The connector's handle is also a little more specialized than you might realize. Can you hear the little micro switch in here when I depress the latch?
cues.zh: 整个单元大概重20磅，也就是约9公斤，但绝大部分重量都来自这根线缆。实际单元只是个塑料盒。连接器本身设计可插拔1万次，这意味着在私人场所能用几十年，在公共场所也至少能用好几年。连接器的手柄也比你想的更精巧。我按下卡扣时，你能听到里面那个小微型开关的声音吗？

cues.en: This actually adds another resistor across the proximity pin and the protective ground, which signals to the car that it's about to be unplugged. This is actually among the most elegant parts of this design spec. More or less the instant the car sees that resistance change, it stops pulling power from the grid.
cues.zh: 这实际上是在接近引脚和保护地之间又加了一个电阻，向汽车发出即将拔枪的信号。这其实是这个设计规范中最精妙的部分之一。汽车几乎在检测到电阻变化的瞬间，就停止从电网取电。

cues.en: That means that when you interrupt a charge by unplugging the connector, current flow has stopped before the pins are actually separated, and indeed before the contactor opens, which prevents arcing and prolongs the life of both connectors and the contactor inside the EVSE. Pretty neat. Now, just because these devices are really quite simple doesn't mean there isn't room for innovation here. The biggest limitation with this standard is that the car can't really communicate with the charger other than to say
cues.zh: 这意味着，当你通过拔下连接器来中断充电时，电流在引脚真正分离之前、甚至在接触器断开之前就已经停止了，从而防止电弧，延长连接器和EVSE内部接触器的寿命。相当巧妙。不过，这些设备虽然很简单，并不意味着没有创新空间。这个标准最大的局限是，汽车除了说

cues.en: Please provide power, and rarely, I need ventilation. There really isn't anything like negotiation going on, and the charger is completely unaware of the characteristics of the car, such as its state of charge, battery capacity, or indeed maximum charging rate. That could be quite useful for things like load sharing and potential backfeeding to the grid should that ever come to fruition. Let's talk about load sharing, because that is a powerful tool for things like multifamily residential situations.
cues.zh: 请供电，以及很少说的“我需要通风”之外，基本无法与充电器通信。根本不存在什么协商，充电器完全不知道汽车的特性，比如荷电状态、电池容量，甚至最大充电速率。这些信息对于负载分配以及未来可能的向电网回馈电都是很有用的。我们来聊聊负载分配，因为对于多户住宅这类场景来说，这是个强大的工具。

cues.en: Here, Tesla currently leads the way by quite a margin. Load sharing allows a given circuit to provide multiple vehicles with electricity by managing the current each vehicle can pull when more than one is plugged in. Say you have a 40-amp circuit like this thing is on. Well, you could put all of the allowed 32 amps continuous into one charging station and thus one vehicle, but you could also share that amongst multiple charging locations.
cues.zh: 在这方面，Tesla目前遥遥领先。负载共享让一条电路能为多辆车供电，方法是当多辆车同时插上时，管理每辆车可拉取的电流。比如说你有一条40安的电路，就像这个。你可以把允许的32安持续电流全部给一个充电站，也就是一辆车，但也可以把它分摊到多个充电位置。

cues.en: See, a 40 amp circuit, like what supplies this, is capable of providing roughly 600 miles of driving range over a 24 hour period. But if you typically drive just 40 miles in a day, you only need about 7% of that output on a typical day. Sharing it among multiple charge points allows for more people to have access to one circuit at the same time.
cues.zh: 你看，像给这个供电的40安电路，在24小时内大约能提供600英里的续航里程。但如果你每天通常只开40英里，那平时你只需要大约7%的输出。把它分摊到多个充电点，就能让更多人同时使用同一条电路。

cues.en: So long as the charge points can talk to each other, they can simply command whatever vehicles are plugged into them to pull less current so that it can be spread out between more vehicles. As individual vehicles are unplugged or finish charging, they will allow the remaining vehicles to pull more current. Now this isn't unique to Tesla, but right now Tesla has the most flexible and also most economical solution available through their quasi-proprietary wall connectors.
cues.zh: 只要充电点之间能互相通信，它们就可以直接命令插着的车辆少拉电流，从而把电流分给更多车辆。当个别车辆拔掉或充完电后，它们会让剩下的车辆拉更多电流。这并不是Tesla独有的，但目前Tesla通过其准专有的壁挂式连接器，提供了最灵活也最经济的方案。

cues.en: Up to 16 Gen 3 wall connectors can share a single circuit and communicate with each other wirelessly, which greatly simplifies installation. While spreading even 60 amps, the max supported by the wall connector, out between 16 cars leaves a paltry sum for each vehicle, the idea isn't really to allow 16 cars to charge at once. It's to allow things like shared parking lots or garages and multifamily dwellings to have more charging points with less capital investment.
cues.zh: 最多16个Gen 3壁挂式连接器可以共享一条电路，并通过无线方式互相通信，这大大简化了安装。虽然把壁挂式连接器支持的最大60安分摊到16辆车，每辆车分到的少得可怜，但这个思路并不是真让16辆车同时充电。而是让共享停车场、车库和多户住宅等场所能用更少的资本投入拥有更多充电点。

cues.en: it is very unlikely that all 16 units will ever be in use at the same time, and Tesla has one other advantage up their sleeve here. Because Tesla is Tesla, they'll have absolutely no reservations about allowing direct communication between the cars and the wall connectors. It's my understanding that the Tesla wall connectors use the same protocol as SAE J1772 in the cable, they just use Tesla's proprietary connector rather than
cues.zh: 16个单元同时使用的情况极不可能发生，而且特斯拉在这方面还有一个优势。因为特斯拉就是特斯拉，他们会毫不犹豫地允许车辆与壁挂式连接器之间直接通信。据我了解，特斯拉壁挂式连接器在电缆中使用的协议与SAE J1772相同，只是使用了特斯拉专有连接器而非

cues.en: the real deal, so I don't think they talk through the charge cable itself. I'm absolutely certain I'll be corrected if I'm wrong, so I won't even bother asking. But the good thing is that this allows non-Tesla vehicles to charge on a Tesla wall connector with an adapter. Thankfully. That's why they're not quite proprietary.
cues.zh: 标准接口，所以我认为它们并非通过充电电缆本身进行通信。如果我错了，肯定会有人纠正我，所以我干脆不问。但好处是，这允许非特斯拉车辆通过适配器在特斯拉壁挂式连接器上充电。谢天谢地，这就是它们不算完全专有的原因。

cues.en: Barely, but if Tesla vehicles can talk to each other and also the network of wall connectors through some other means like WiFi, they can communicate their states of charge, and rather than split the available current equally, it can be prioritized to vehicles with lower charge. From my perusal of the manual of the Gen 3 wall connector, it doesn't look like this prioritization feature is currently live, but of course there's no reason to think it won't be quite soon via a firmware update.
cues.zh: 勉强算是，但如果特斯拉车辆能通过WiFi等其他方式相互通信，并与壁挂式连接器网络通信，它们就能传递充电状态，而且不是平均分配可用电流，而是优先分配给电量较低的车辆。从我翻阅第三代壁挂式连接器手册来看，这个优先级功能目前似乎还未启用，但当然，没有理由认为它不会很快通过固件更新实现。

cues.en: Still though, similar solutions are available from companies like Clipper Creek, and indeed, inside the Siemens unit there are some connections which make me think it can be bonded to other units and even limit its charge rate based on a little potentiometer I saw in there, but anyway, those companies don't have the advantage of vertical integration, and so their products tend to be a little more expensive. That's the downside of serving everybody and not perpetuating a walled garden. Plus, right now, there's no codified state of charge communication between car and EVSE.
cues.zh: 尽管如此，类似方案也可从Clipper Creek等公司获得，而且事实上，西门子设备内部有一些连接让我觉得它可以与其他单元连接，甚至根据我看到的一个小电位器来限制充电速率，但无论如何，那些公司没有垂直整合的优势，所以他们的产品往往稍贵一些。这就是服务所有人而非维护封闭生态系统的劣势。此外，目前车辆与EVSE之间还没有标准化的充电状态通信。

cues.en: However, that could change. A proposed update to the SAE J1772 standard, really would have been nice to have given it some sort of name, guys, would enable real vehicle to charger integration using power line communication protocols. That would help enable my personal EV charging pipe dream. I would love for power utilities to start installing their own level 2 EVSE equipment all over the place.
cues.zh: 不过，这种情况可能会改变。SAE J1772标准的一项拟议更新——说实话，当初要是给它起个名字就好了，伙计们——将能通过电力线通信协议实现真正的车辆与充电器集成。那将有助于实现我个人的电动汽车充电梦想。我非常希望电力公司能开始到处安装他们自己的二级EVSE设备。

cues.en: help get people in apartment buildings set up, and those who live in areas with on-street parking only. If the car could communicate with the EVSE, and the EVSE as part of a smart grid, an EV driver can register their car, plug it in anywhere on the network, and have the electricity it uses automatically added to their own personal electric bill. Public charging today is a mess of competing companies each trying to make a profit in one way or another, and maybe that's where we should go, but personally,
cues.zh: 帮助公寓楼里的人安装好，还有那些住在只有路边停车位区域的人。如果汽车能与EVSE通信，而EVSE又作为智能电网的一部分，电动汽车司机就可以注册他们的车，插到网络中任何地方，所用的电就会自动加到他们个人的电费账单上。今天的公共充电是一团乱麻，各家公司互相竞争，各自想方设法赚钱，也许这就是我们该走的路，但就我个人而言，

cues.en: I kind of wish utilities would just step in. Plus, if the car can tell the grid its state of charge, dynamic load balancing on a huge scale would be easy to implement without stranding drivers. And should backfeeding of the car's charge to the grid ever be a thing? Well that's a perfect way to make that happen. If you're a policy maker, and or someone who works for a utility, I'd just like to say I really think you ought to start looking at this. If you had level 2 chargers everywhere,
cues.zh: 我有点希望电力公司能直接介入。另外，如果汽车能告诉电网它的充电状态，大规模动态负载平衡就能轻松实现，而不会让司机陷入困境。如果汽车的电力回馈给电网有一天真能实现呢？那这正是实现它的完美方式。如果你是政策制定者，或者为电力公司工作，我只想说，我真的认为你们应该开始关注这件事。如果到处都有二级充电器，

cues.en: You incentivize people to keep their cars plugged in, and if their cars are able to feed the grid in times of excess demand, well, now you have access to battery storage which you didn't need to pay for.
cues.zh: 你就能激励人们让车一直插着电，如果他们的车能在需求过剩时向电网供电，那么，你现在就拥有了无需付费的电池储能。

cues.en: And yes, I know that idea is unsettling to many people, but the beauty of a smart grid is that you could potentially offer incentives and opt people in, or you could simply codify into vehicle design that every EV has a 10% charge buffer that's invisible to the driver. That way there's some battery capacity that they don't even know they have and never affects their range. There's so much we could do, all it takes is some imagination and willingness to regulate some things.
cues.zh: 是的，我知道这个想法让很多人不安，但智能电网的妙处在于，你可以提供激励、让人们选择加入，也可以直接写进车辆设计规范：每辆电动汽车都保留 10% 的电量缓冲，司机察觉不到。这样电池里就有一部分容量他们根本不知道，也永远不会影响续航。我们能做的很多，只需要一点想象力和监管一些事情的意愿。

cues.en: which is obviously a pretty tough sell in the US at present. But for now, your Garden Variety EVSE is a pretty dumb device. Even Tesla's wall connectors when installed individually really don't do anything more than this does. If I can give a piece of advice to those who are in a situation where they can install their own charger in a private garage, it would be this. Have an electrician install a NEMA 650 receptacle. I installed this one myself, and yes, I know that needs to be in conduit,
cues.zh: 显然，这在美国目前很难让人接受。但眼下，普通的 EVSE 是个相当“笨”的设备。就连 Tesla 的壁挂式连接器，单独安装时，也真不比这个多做多少事。如果我能给那些能在私人车库安装自己充电器的人一点建议，那就是：让电工装一个 NEMA 650 插座。这个是我自己装的，是的，我知道这得穿管，

cues.en: I'm getting to it. Anyway, many EVSEs are available with this plug, and they come in various capacities. It will allow effortless changes in the future, and also offers some peace of mind in case your EVSE happens to develop a fault of some kind and becomes unusable. Then you could simply replace it yourself in mere moments. Though as I hope I've shown you, there really isn't much that can go wrong with these. It's just a fancy light switch.
cues.zh: 我正要说这个。总之，很多 EVSE 都带这种插头，而且有各种功率规格。以后想换设备会很方便，万一你的 EVSE 出了某种故障、不能用了，也能让你安心些。那样你很快就能自己换掉。不过，希望我已经说明了，这些设备其实没多少会出问题的地方。它就是个花哨的电灯开关。

cues.en: Thanks for watching. I hope with this video I've explained that this piece of the EV puzzle is actually quite simple. There's a lot more we could do, and in my opinion should do, to make EVs more feasible for more people and to help leverage them as much as possible. The real challenge is how to get EV charging more accessible to renters, multifamily dwellings, and areas with street parking only.
cues.zh: 感谢观看。希望这个视频已经说清楚了，电动车这个难题中的这一环其实很简单。我们还能做很多事，而且我认为也应该做，让电动车对更多人更可行，帮助尽可能发挥它们的作用。真正的挑战在于，如何让租户、多户住宅以及只有路边停车的地区更容易用上电动车充电。

cues.en: Tesla deserves praise for their innovation with the wall connector, but I do hope they will eventually join the rest of the automotive industry and remove the dichotomy in North American charging standards that as of 2020, they alone are maintaining for a competitive advantage.
cues.zh: Tesla 在壁挂式充电连接器上的创新值得称赞，但我确实希望他们最终能加入其他汽车厂商的行列，消除北美充电标准中的分裂局面——截至 2020 年，只有 Tesla 一家为了竞争优势还在维持这种分裂。

cues.en: I know, I can't help myself here, but I say that not necessarily to disparage Tesla, but to let the less familiar with the EV world know that an industry standard charging protocol and connector exists for all vehicles not made by Tesla.
cues.zh: 我知道，我在这儿忍不住要说，但我这么说倒不一定是想贬低 Tesla，而是想让不太熟悉电动车领域的人知道，存在一套适用于所有非 Tesla 车辆的行业标准充电协议和连接器。

cues.en: and also to get some of the more die-hard Tesla fans to engage with that reality and what that might mean for the future adoption of electric vehicles. Yes, you may wish to bring up that Tesla went their own way because the standards we have now were not yet finalized, and they totally should have. EVs would not be taken seriously were it not for the Supercharger network. But a robust standard exists now that every manufacturer has signed onto.
cues.zh: 同时也是想让一些更铁杆的 Tesla 粉丝正视这个现实，以及这对未来电动车普及可能意味着什么。是的，你可能会说 Tesla 当初另起炉灶是因为现在的标准当时还没定稿，他们完全应该那么做。要不是有 Supercharger 网络，电动车不会被认真对待。但现在已经有了一个健全的标准，而且每家厂商都签了字。

cues.en: They owe it not just to future Tesla owners, but also the industry as a whole to support it. And better do it now than later. Just for context, that little orange thing below this charge port, that covers the high-powered DC pins of this CCS combo connector.
cues.zh: 他们这样做不仅是为了未来的特斯拉车主，也是为了整个行业。而且宜早不宜迟。简单说明一下，充电口下方那个橙色的小东西，覆盖着这个CCS组合连接器的高功率直流插针。

cues.en: Again, every modern EV and plug-in hybrid going back to 2010, except for Tesla's, has a J1772 connector. And by augmenting it with these large DC pins, DC fast charging was added without removing compatibility with existing level 1 and 2 AC infrastructure. Now that Nissan has dropped the competing Chatham-O from the US market, every new EV will soon have this exact plug, or it will be a Tesla.
cues.zh: 再次说明，从2010年起，每辆现代电动车和插电式混合动力车，除了特斯拉之外，都配有J1772连接器。通过增加这些大型直流插针，就增加了直流快充功能，同时不失去对现有1级和2级交流基础设施的兼容性。既然日产已将竞争性的Chatham-O撤出美国市场，很快每辆新电动车都将配备这个插头，否则就是特斯拉。

cues.en: And don't tell Tesla loyalists, but these bigger pins, which they often like to say make the connector needlessly bulky, can handle more current than Tesla's proprietary connector. If Tesla chooses to support CCS in the North American market as they have already done in Europe and China, I will be so delighted I'll make a video about just that. But!
